questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation
questions.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-y \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2\cdot x+(-1)\cdot y \\ 1\cdot x+(-1)\cdot y\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2x-y \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$

    Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T,$ find $T(v).$

| $T(v)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}18 \\ -6 \\ 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2y-5z+x \\ z-y+3x \\ -z-2x+3y\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, rewrite the order of the variables in the usual way:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}]
$$

We require a $3\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
